title: Audit and Troubleshooting
summary: Provides methods to investigate anomalies, verify data health, and resolve common operational issues.
coverage: Detecting inconsistent records or test states

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Audit and troubleshooting should preserve evidence before remediation. Export relevant datasets and capture timestamps before destructive changes.

sections.title: First-response workflow
paragraphs: Use a fixed triage sequence to reduce false assumptions and shorten recovery time. Start from scope and symptom, then validate session state, permission state, and data state in order.
Do not begin with direct database edits. Most issues are caused by access controls, assignment rules, stale sessions, or unsaved workflow state.
orderedList: Classify the issue as access, data integrity, workflow, or reporting output.
Capture impacted user, record id, route, and exact response message or HTTP code.
Check `GET /session-status` for login state and remaining session windows.
Confirm effective permissions and role for the impacted account.
Validate object-level constraints such as pentest assignment ownership.
Apply corrective action and verify end-to-end behavior on the same object.

sections.title: Session and authentication triage
paragraphs: RAPTOR enforces both idle and active timeout windows. Session extension is explicit and capped by extension limits. Login additionally uses lockout counters with escalating lockout windows.
When diagnosing login failures, always distinguish invalid credentials (`401`) from lockout (`429`) and reset-required state (`password_reset_required`).

rows: Verify username normalization and auth source (`local` or LDAP).
Wait for lockout expiry or reset lockout state via controlled admin procedure.
Complete reset endpoint flow before normal route access.
Re-authenticate and continue with fresh session tracking.

sections.title: Data consistency checks
paragraphs: Consistency checks should focus on relationships between records, pentest rows, and generated outputs. Inconsistencies usually appear as missing references, stale labels, or lifecycle conflicts.
Use read-only inspection first, then correct from normal product flows where possible.

sections.title: Audit evidence package checklist
paragraphs: For internal audit and post-incident review, package evidence in a repeatable format so outcomes can be verified independently.
orderedList: Issue statement with impacted modules, users, and object identifiers.
Request and response samples including status codes and timestamps.
Session status snapshot before and after remediation.
Relevant configuration snapshot such as role and optional permissions.
Data exports used for verification, including pre-change and post-change views.
Final validation result and operator sign-off.
